definitions.explanation: A residence other than one's main home. Can refer to a secondary house maintained for work, family reasons, or personal circumstances. Sometimes carries the connotation of a dwelling kept for a mistress or secret relationship.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{都内|とない}に{別宅|べったく}を{持|も}っている。
examples.english: He has a separate residence in central Tokyo.

examples.japanese: {仕事|しごと}の{関係|かんけい}で{会社|かいしゃ}の{近|ちか}くに{別宅|べったく}を{借|か}りた。
examples.english: I rented a second home near the office for work reasons.

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}は{晩年|ばんねん}、{静|しず}かな{田舎|いなか}の{別宅|べったく}で{過|す}ごすことが{多|おお}かった。
examples.english: In his later years, my grandfather often spent time at his separate residence in the quiet countryside.

notes:
A compound of {別|べつ} (separate, different) and {宅|たく} (residence). Unlike {別荘|べっそう} (vacation home), {別宅|べったく} implies a practical secondary residence rather than a leisure property.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {別宅|べったく}を{構|かま}える — to set up a separate residence
- {別宅|べったく}を{持|も}つ — to have a second home
- {別宅|べったく}に{住|す}む — to live at a separate residence

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {別荘|べっそう} — vacation home, villa; used for leisure and relaxation, typically in resort areas
- {自宅|じたく} — one's own home (primary residence)
- {本宅|ほんたく} — main residence (as opposed to a secondary one)
- セカンドハウス — second house (loanword, more neutral and modern)

USAGE:
In some contexts, {別宅|べったく} carries an implication that the separate residence is maintained for a secret romantic relationship, especially in older or literary usage. The phrase {別宅|べったく}を{持|も}つ can be a euphemism for keeping a mistress. In modern usage, however, it often simply means a secondary residence for practical purposes like commuting.
